h: Swapping Ghost Walks for Gutter Balls
p: York is a city of walls, gates and wonderfully odd street names, and the Stonebow sits close to one of the best of them: Whip-Ma-Whop-Ma-Gate, which locals will happily tell you is one of the shortest streets in the city with one of the longest names. It's that kind of place. Every corner has a story, and after a day of hearing them, a few frames of bowling is a welcome change of pace.

Getting here on foot from most of the centre is a doddle. The Stonebow runs along the edge of the old core, so it's handy whether you're coming from the Minster end, Parliament Street or the Hungate side by the River Foss. If you're arriving by train, the walk across the river and through the city takes in some lovely views, so build in a bit of extra time to dawdle.

York gets very busy, especially on race days, weekends and around Christmas when the markets are on. Groups planning a celebration in town should think about booking early, and maybe aim for an earlier slot so you're not competing with every hen party in Yorkshire for a lane. Comfortable shoes are a must for the cobbles on the way, even if you'll be swapping into bowling shoes when you arrive.

After your games, the city is lovely at night. The city walls close at dusk, but the streets around the Minster are atmospheric after dark, and the riverside by Lendal and Ouse bridges makes for a calm stroll back to your hotel or the station.
